etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English squachen, squatchen, from Old French esquacher, escachier, from Vulgar Latin *excoāctiāre, from Latin ex + coāctāre. Probably influenced by Middle English quashen, quassen, from Old French esquasser, escasser (“to crush, shatter, destroy, break”), from Vulgar Latin *exquassare, from Latin ex- + quassare (“to shatter”) (see quash).

definitions.definition: (uncountable) A sport played in a walled court with a soft rubber ball and bats like tennis racquets.

quote.citation: 1922, Michael Arlen, “3/19/2”, in “Piracy”: A Romantic Chronicle of These Days‎[2]:
quote.text: Ivor had acquired more than a mile of fishing rights with the house; he was not at all a good fisherman, but one must do something; one generally, however, banged a ball with a squash-racket against a wall.

definitions.definition: A non-alcoholic drink made from a fruit-based concentrate diluted with water or milk.

quote.citation: 2006 Feb. 17, Graham Linehan, The IT Crowd, Season 1, Episode 4:
quote.text: Sure. I pour hot squash all over myself and we all have a good chuckle. Everyone except Muggins here.

definitions.definition: A place or a situation where people have limited space to move.
(biology) A preparation made by placing material on a slide (flat, rectangular piece of glass), covering it and applying pressure.[1]
(obsolete, countable) Something soft and easily crushed; especially, an unripe pod of peas.
(obsolete, countable, derogatory) Something unripe or soft.
(obsolete, countable) A sudden fall of a heavy, soft body; also, a shock of soft bodies.
(slang, professional wrestling) An extremely one-sided, usually short, match.

quote.citation: Orr, James (2014 August 18) “WWE SummerSlam 2014: How Twitter reacted to John Cena vs Brock Lesnar”, in (Please provide the book title or journal name)‎[3], The Independent, retrieved 30 July 2015
quote.text: It was one of the most shocking WWE title matches ever witnessed, and effectively a 20-minute squash match as Brock Lesnar "conquered" his opponent.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To beat or press into pulp or a flat mass; to crush.
(transitive, intransitive) To compress or restrict (oneself) into a small space; to squeeze.
(transitive) To suppress; to force into submission.

quote.citation: 2006, Chris Rodda, Liars for Jesus, →ISBN, page 390:
quote.text: A somewhat popular myth about the Whiskey Rebellion is that Washington personally led the troops into western Pennsylvania and squashed the rebellion.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: Shortening of Narragansett askutasquash (“[a vegetable] eaten green (or raw)”), from askut (“green, raw”) +‎ asquash (“eaten”).

definitions.definition: Cucurbita maxima, including hubbard squash, great winter squash, buttercup squash, and some varieties of pumpkins.
Cucurbita argyrosperma (syn. Cucurbita mixta), cushaw squash.
Cucurbita moschata, butternut squash, Barbary squash, China squash.
Cucurbita pepo, most pumpkins, acorn squash, summer squash, zucchini.
(botany, countable) A plant and its fruit of any of a few species of the genus Cucurbita, or gourd kind.
Lagenaria siceraria (syn. Cucurbita verrucosa), calabash, long-neck squash.
(botany) Any other similar-looking plant of other genera.
(cooking) The edible or decorative fruit of these plants, or this fruit prepared as a dish.
(obsolete, countable) Muskrat.

quote.citation: 1705, William Dampier, A Supplement of the Voyage Round the World:
quote.text: The squash is a four-footed beast, bigger than a cat.
